solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old socialite facing endless danger? Rubbish!

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a deb (debutante) was a young society woman making her entrance
a synonym for danger

explanation.surface: An outraged reader dismisses the idea that some aging society lady is in peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' just places the socialite before the danger; the last letter of the danger word is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste and broken remains, a close synonym for rubbish as a noun.

clue.text: Dutiful editor in charge, old-fashioned on the outside

indicators.note: being on the outside means wrapping around the other pieces

parts.note: something dated is out of fashion
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A conscientious, rather old-fashioned editor runs the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dedicated is committed and devoted to their work, close in sense to dutiful and conscientious.

clue.text: Dangerous device on a street makes one rant

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive device
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An explosive left in the road provokes someone into a furious tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated speech, and a rant is loud overblown talk, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Slight gains ultimately reduced all round

indicators.note: trimming the words at both ends leaves a run of letters from their middle

parts.note: drop the outer letters of these two words and read straight across the gap

explanation.surface: Modest profits were eventually cut across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight gains' reads as small profits, but Slight is a verb or noun meaning a snub; the answer sits inside the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or affront, and an insult is a remark or act that offends, so the two coincide.

clue.text: Calling social worker to meet reticent person

parts.note: someone who clams up is called a clam
the ant is a social insect and a worker, a classic crossword trick

explanation.surface: A council social worker is sent to visit someone who will not talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a job title, but it is an insect from a colony; the reticent person comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant is a literary adjective for clamouring or crying out insistently, so a calling voice fits it.

clue.text: Notice soldiers under colonel initially, a small fighting force?

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means placed below, so the pieces follow on
initially points to taking only the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the opening letter of colonel
an ad is a notice in a paper
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An advertisement for troops placed beneath a colonel's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small trained core group, often of military officers, around which a larger unit is built.

clue.text: Taking care of boy in a church is an honour

parts.note: surface padding that turns the abbreviation into a phrase about looking after someone
taken as written

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Looking after a boy in church is a great privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking care of' sounds like looking after, but only 'care of' gives letters; 'Taking' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, a mark of distinction that amounts to an honour.

clue.text: Go in van around French city

indicators.note: letters moved around are put into a fresh order

parts.note: the three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to tour a city in France by van.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a city in Provence in southern France, once the seat of the popes.

clue.text: Numbers with minimal English — something they need to learn about?

definitions.text: something they need to learn about?

parts.note: tens are numbers

indicators.note: minimal means the least possible, so just one letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of English

explanation.surface: Students with poor English struggling with their arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' are the students with minimal English, who must learn verb tenses as part of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners of English must master verb forms showing past, present and future time, so this grammar topic is required study.

clue.text: Criticise the performing group of all-time greats?

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
taken as written
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: A critic slates a band of legendary performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the set of most revered figures in a field, like the gods of a temple.

clue.text: The people in protests briefly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek word for the common populace, used in English
second meaning: the casual short form of demonstrations, plural

explanation.surface: Ordinary citizens briefly take to the streets in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Demos names a citizen body in political writing, and also serves as a clipped plural for public marches and rallies.

clue.text: Act bound to be bad with one being captured?

definitions.text: Act bound to be bad with one being captured?

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so one piece sits within the rest
letters that go bad are spoiled and disordered, so they get rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An act that is bound to be wicked, with someone held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a wicked act in which a person is captured is exactly a kidnapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction is the crime of seizing and carrying someone off, an act in which one person is held captive.

clue.text: Girl in daily prize draw losing track

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char(woman)

indicators.note: losing something means letting it go, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a draw for prizes
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A girl enters a newspaper's daily prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper, but in British usage a daily is a cleaning lady; the railway abbreviation comes off the end of the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte is a common female first name, and crosswords often define given names simply as girl or boy.

clue.text: Weapon knight's hidden in fine material

indicators.note: something hidden in another thing is tucked inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight's weapon is concealed under delicate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' tempts a hunt for a word buried in the letters, but here it places the chess knight inside the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is the long spear carried by mounted knights in jousting and cavalry charges.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval you heard for skimpy garment

parts.note: the click of the tongue people make when disapproving

indicators.note: what is heard is going by sound, so a letter that sounds like the word is used

parts.note: the letter name is said exactly like this word

explanation.surface: Someone tuts disapprovingly at a scanty outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt worn by ballet dancers, a very brief piece of clothing.

clue.text: Family needing inner energy eats plants

indicators.note: needing something inner means it must be put inside, so a piece goes within

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
E is the symbol for energy
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A household that needs energy from within sits down to a vegetable meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' sits at the end looking like what is being eaten, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Celandines are small yellow-flowered wild plants of the buttercup and poppy families.

clue.text: Deeply interested brothers sitting up in a bunk maybe

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the bed

parts.note: a bunk is an example of a bed, hence maybe

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: BROS is the abbreviation for brothers

explanation.surface: Siblings sit up in bunk beds, deeply engrossed in something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being absorbed in something means being engrossed and wholly occupied by it.

clue.text: Like sheep and goats, extremes in some Bible story

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of some
a parable is a moral story told by Jesus

explanation.surface: Sheep and goats appear in a famous Bible tale.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew's gospel the sheep are divided from the goats at the Last Judgement, so they can be told apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Separable means able to be divided, as the flock is split into two groups at judgement.

clue.text: Guide needing to conceal untruth? That's harder

indicators.note: to conceal something you hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to steer is to guide
a lie is an untruth

explanation.surface: A guide must hide a falsehood, and finds that tougher.
explanation.definitionFit: Steelier is the comparative of steely, so it means more like steel, tougher or more resolute.

clue.text: Delicacy isn't fashionable in attire — not right!

indicators.note: in places the earlier words inside the clothing word
saying not right asks for the abbreviation for right to be removed

parts.note: dress means clothing
what is in is in fashion
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Being dainty is out of fashion, especially in clothes that are not right.
explanation.definitionFit: Daintiness is the quality of being delicate and refined, so delicacy is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bill's trendy way of speaking

parts.note: what is in is fashionable
a voice is a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill has a fashionable manner of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is a request for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a document requesting payment for goods or services, which is what a bill is.

clue.text: Secure provincial party with nothing smuggled in

indicators.note: goods smuggled in are slipped inside secretly, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, often called the Province
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A regional political party has nothing sneaked through its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'the Province' means Northern Ireland, whose DUP is a major party.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up a coat or buckle is to fasten it, so the phrasal verb means to make secure.

clue.text: Commander to be facing resistance in time of revolution

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding
taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A commander must face up to resistance during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian Revolution of 1917 is called the October Revolution, so the month is the period of that uprising.

clue.text: Attack quietly with little weight

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: An assault made softly and with very little force behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly on prey or an enemy, a sudden attack.

clue.text: Second contest in film

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: A runner-up finish in a competition shown on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie is the everyday American word for a cinema picture, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Miseries of work, being surrounded by endless muddle

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting inside another piece
something endless is missing its final part, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
an op (opus) is a work

explanation.surface: The unhappiness of work buried in never-ending chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopes are gloomy, sulky people, and miseries is the informal British word for such complainers.

clue.text: Gee — a right baddy!

parts.note: gee is the spoken name of the letter G
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
a rotter is a cad or villain

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at meeting a real villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the exclamation describes the answer: a strangler is certainly a right baddy.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotter strangles victims with a cord or wire, which makes such a person a thoroughly wicked villain.

clue.text: Learner in good Scottish organisation

indicators.note: in places the learner sign inside the Scots word

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A trainee joins a fine Scottish body.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is an association of craftsmen or merchants, a formally constituted organisation.

clue.text: Proper drink I have, being unsophisticated

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone admits to taking a respectable drink, which shows a lack of sophistication.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth, so It stands for the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive describes something crude, simple or undeveloped, which is the sense of unsophisticated as an adjective.

clue.text: Grab old boy to become overseas ruler

parts.note: to nab is to seize
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil is seized and made a foreign potentate.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob was a Muslim governor in Mughal India, so the title names a ruler in a distant land.

clue.text: The woman, a lefty that's somehow sheep-like?

parts.note: the pronoun for a woman
taken as written
a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A left-wing woman is mocked for following the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheep-like' suggests timid conformity, but the question mark points to what is done to sheep: their fleece is clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are routinely clipped of wool, so having been sheared is one way of being like a sheep.

clue.text: Get less, having cancelled a second order

indicators.note: cancelled items are struck out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to decrease is to become less
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone receives less after a second order is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official ruling or command, which is order in its sense of an instruction.
